summary.headline: Management flagged a 9% QoQ fall in Q4 export volume (44,500 MT vs 48,900 MT) from war-stranded shipments, and declined to quantify the Q1 spillover.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a profitable year and declared a dividend of INR 3 per share, but the transcript contains no reported P&L figures beyond the Q4 export volume. Management attributed FY26 gains to buying paddy/rice inventory when prices were low, and said prices have since risen about 30% from Nov-Dec to March. The West Asia conflict slowed shipments to Iran, Afghanistan (via Bandar Abbas) and some Iraqi ports, while Red Sea, Jordan (Aqaba), Egypt, Oman, Dubai and Saudi (Jeddah) routes continued. Freight and insurance increases are said to be passed through to buyers, with ECGC claims filed for extra war charges. Management declined to quantify Q1 spillover or EBITDA margin for Q1 and repeatedly said it was too early to comment on El Nino impact.

financial_highlights.change: -9% QoQ from 48,900 MT (per analyst's figures; management confirmed a 9% drop)
increase, as stated by Gaurav Mahy (comparison period not fully specified)

financial_highlights.metric: Rice price move since Nov-Dec to March

segments.name: Rice exports
segments.commentary: Core business, shipped to about 100 countries; Middle East, Europe, US, Canada and Australia cited as active. Management said the company is betting mainly on continued rice export growth.

segments.name: Domestic branded / e-commerce
segments.commentary: Brand sold in 40-45 countries; Indian sales limited to online portals and e-commerce (Blinkit, Amazon in Gurgaon/NCR). Management plans to expand territories and tie up domestic distributors; no revenue figure given.

segments.name: New manufacturing units
segments.commentary: Three new units installed and operating at about 50% of normal efficiency; management estimated each unit could generate INR 15-20 crore of sales per month at full run.

guidance_outlook: Management said Q1 volumes should be fairly normal, and the Q4 shortfall from stranded containers will be executed in Q1 (quantum not disclosed).
Management declined to give Q1 EBITDA margin guidance, saying it was premature while ocean freight is high.
Ankit Setia said upcoming quarters would be similar in profitability to FY26, though he did not give numbers.
Potential new large Saudi importer (2-2.5 lakh MT annual requirement) visiting Karnal and Gujarat units; could add 30,000-40,000 MT, with a 40,000-50,000 MT opportunity cited.
Management said it is looking at FY27 as a possible growth inflection after roughly three years of flat revenue at INR 1,400-1,500 crore, without giving a number.
Working capital cycle target is 40-45 days per Rajeev Setia, but management said it would maintain the current cycle.
capex_capacity: Three new units installed; operating at about 50% of normal efficiency.
Each new unit could generate about INR 15-20 crore of sales a month at full run.
Factories cited in Karnal (Haryana) and Gujarat.
Company said it has funds for domestic brand expansion; no capex amount given.
Management said the company has large cash reserves; an analyst requested a share buyback, which management did not address.
demand_pricing: Rice export prices up ~30% from Nov-Dec to March; management said Q4 realisations were high and it has stock bought at low prices.
Freight and war-risk insurance costs are said to be borne by importers and built into prices; initially some was absorbed by the company.
Afghanistan demand rising after Afghanistan-Pakistan trade issues, but shipments via Bandar Abbas are slow due to the war.
Jordan volumes up as Iraq's Umm Qasr port is not functional; cargo is rerouted via Aqaba.
Management said there is no dumping from other countries, since Basmati is produced only in India; no shipments are currently stuck.
Industry exports cited at about 6-6.5 million tons (figures inconsistent during the call).

qa_highlights.question: How has the Iran war affected rice realisations and shipping disruption in March-May?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Setia said the impact exists but routes are open via Red Sea, Dubai, Khor Fakkan, Fujairah and Oman, with extra war charges claimed from ECGC. Ocean freight is higher but passed through to buyers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected EBITDA margin for Q1 FY27 given higher freight?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is premature to comment on margins, with business continuing and demand for essentials holding up.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 the next inflection point for revenue, after about 3-4 years at INR 1,400-1,500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Setia said cargo is still moving and that history shows growth after roughly three years of flat revenue; a large buyer is due to visit the factory the following week.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin profile structural or cyclical, and what happens if realisations fall 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin to buying inventory at low prices early in the season, with godowns full. It did not give a sensitivity to a 10% realisation fall.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital cycle target?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Setia said the target is a maximum of 40-45 days. The moderator cited the current cycle at about 190 days (60 debtor days, 140 inventory days), and management said it would maintain it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 export volume fall about 9% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Mahy attributed the drop to shipments stuck en route due to the Iran conflict. The moderator said containers would be executed in Q1, and Gaurav confirmed the issue is resolved.

risks_watch: Q4 export volume fell 9% QoQ due to stranded shipments; the Q1 spillover is unquantified.
Shipping costs and slow delivery to Iran and Afghanistan (via Bandar Abbas) due to the West Asia conflict.
Paddy crop size risk from a possible El Nino; management said it is too early to assess and paddy comes in Oct-Nov.
Margin sustainability: management said it is premature to say whether Q4 margins can be held in Q1 FY27.
Inventory-heavy model with about 190-day working capital cycle versus a stated 40-45 day target.
Customer concentration: top 10 customers at about 35% of revenue (management unsure of figure).
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on FY26 profits and the price-driven inventory gains, but evasive on forward quarters, Q1 margins, the spillover quantum and El Nino impact, often saying it is 'premature'. Several answers were given with hesitation and internal cross-referencing, and figures such as top-10 customer share and industry exports were not firmly stated.
key_quotes: And you see, there has been 30% increase in prices from November, December to March.
And they are visiting our factory shortly next week.
So, our margins remain same based on the market prices, the markets have gone up and similarly, we have also adjusted our prices.
My closing comments would be that this year has been really great.
